subject: Next steps: air-gapped on‑prem qualification & dry‑run scheduling
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Kim <andrew.kim@novagen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: air-gapped qualification — quick list of asks

Hi Andrew —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a short list of items we need to qualify to size the on‑prem/private deployment and propose a dry‑run window: 

1) Hardware & connectivity
- Confirm whether the target rack(s) will have air‑gapped jump host(s) for package transfers or if all updates must be done via removable media.
- Any constraints on allowed toolchains (e.g., no outbound HTTPS, only signed RPMs)?

2) Maintenance & upgrades
- Typical maintenance window(s) and preferred blackout periods.
- Do you require Redwood to perform offline firmware/BIOS updates, or will Novagen handle firmware updates?

3) Spares & logistics
- Preferred level of on‑site spares (N+1 vs. N+2) and whether Novagen has a local support partner for same‑day hardware swaps.

4) Security & key management
- KMS/HSM requirements for private key material and whether keys must be held in customer HSM.

5) Dry‑run:
- We propose a short, tracked dry‑run (non‑production) to validate install, patch flow, and backup/restore. Please share a few candidate weeks (Feb–Mar) and whether Novagen can commit to a 2–3 day window with an on‑site engineer.

Attachments: I can share a lightweight BOM template and a preliminary SOW draft for your procurement team once we lock the scope.

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above and a preferred dry‑run week, we’ll prepare a Tech Deep Dive invite (30–60m) and circulate the BOM/SOW.

Best,

Elliot Price
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Andrew Kim <andrew.kim@novagen.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Mira Patel <mira.patel@novagen.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: air-gapped qualification — quick list of asks

Elliot — thanks for the summary. Quick answers and clarifications below.

1) Connectivity: Novagen facilities are fully air‑gapped. We have an approved jump host process managed by our infra team; transfers are done over encrypted removable media or via a controlled sneakernet procedure. No outbound HTTPS allowed from the target cluster.

2) Toolchains: We can accept signed RPMs and vendor‑signed installers. We cannot allow container pulls from external registries at deploy time.

3) Maintenance windows: Our weekly maintenance window is Saturday 02:00–06:00 local. We prefer upgrades to happen during that slot; emergency patches are scheduled in coordination with the platform owner.

4) Spares: We maintain N+1 for GPUs and networking; we do not have a local swap partner. We will need Redwood to advise on minimum spares for 48‑hour RTO.

5) KMS: Keys must be customer‑managed. We can integrate with HSM via an offline attestation workflow — need to see Redwood’s proposed approach.

Dry‑run: We can do a dry‑run week of Mar 8–12 or Mar 22–26. On‑site engineer availability is limited but possible for a 48‑hour window.

Can you send the BOM template and the SOW draft to our procurement lead (cc’d Mira)? She’ll need the procurement contact and estimated lead times for any ordered spares.

Thanks,

Andrew
Senior Infrastructure Manager
Novagen Therapeutics
andrew.kim@novagen.com

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Kim <andrew.kim@novagen.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: air-gapped qualification — quick list of asks

Andrew — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the candidate dry‑run windows. I’m Marissa (Solution Lead) — copying Ben (Field Ops) to scope spares and on‑site logistics.

What I’m attaching here:
- network-diagram.pdf (stub) — lightweight template to confirm network boundaries, jump host placement, and physical rack mapping.
- sow-draft-v0.3.docx (stub) — initial SOW with a conservative timeline and dry‑run activities called out.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Procurement contact for lead times / purchase order routing (Mira is cc’d).
- Confirmation if Novagen requires Redwood to manage firmware updates during dry‑run or if Novagen will stage firmware beforehand.
- A contact for the local facilities team to coordinate physical access and spares staging (if Novagen wants Redwood to ship spares and label them for on‑site swap).

Proposed plan:
1) Tech Deep Dive (60m) week of Feb 22 — we’ll bring the tech leads and an offline patch-flow demo (video + written MOP).
2) Lock dry‑run week: we’ll tentatively hold Mar 8–12 pending procurement confirmation.

If that works, we’ll update the SOW with confirmed dates and an estimated spares SKU list (Ben will follow up on quantity and lead times).

Thanks — I’ll also drop a short recorded video of our offline patch flow for your team to review before the Deep Dive.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (stub), sow-draft-v0.3.docx (stub)

Andrew — Ben here. Thanks — Mar 8–12 is doable; we’ll tentatively reserve that window and start compiling an initial spares list.

Quick Q: who should I loop in for purchase orders and customs (if we need to ship spares into CA)? Mira, can you confirm procurement contact and any required vendor onboarding docs?

I’ll aim to have a preliminary spare‑SKU list and lead times by Feb 20 so procurement can lock shipping windows. Also we’ll prepare a short MOP checklist for the dry‑run and share ahead of time.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
